parts:
Thanks Luis ,

The AvgPIC statistics works and i  have also need your suggestion regarding   Botstein et al. (1980) PIC,  PIC = 1 − (p² + q²) − 2p²q², which gave me different PIC value as below

head(gl6$other$loc.metrics$AvgPIC)
[1] 0.3207420 0.2054814 0.1142745 0.1331487 0.1591401
[6] 0.2596838
> pic <- gl6$other$loc.metrics$AvgPIC
> summary(pic)
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
0.09095 0.21039 0.33972 0.32507 0.45088 0.49988 
> allele_freq <- gl.alf(gl6)
> head(allele_freq)   # columns: alf1 (p), alf2 (q)  -- p + q = 1
                      alf1       alf2
100049933-25-T/C 0.7990196 0.20098039
100050483-7-A/G  0.8835979 0.11640212
100050564-43-A/G 0.9391534 0.06084656
100050612-64-A/G 0.9282178 0.07178218
100050665-46-A/G 0.9127907 0.08720930
100050761-64-C/T 0.8455882 0.15441176
> # Observed heterozygosity per locus:
> # In dartR 0/1/2 coding, genotype score == 1 is heterozygous
> geno_mat <- as.matrix(gl6)   # individuals x loci, values 0/1/2/NA
> Ho_locus <- apply(geno_mat, 2, function(x) {
+   mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
+ })
> # Expected heterozygosity (gene diversity) per locus: He = 2pq
> He_locus <- 2 * allele_freq$alf1 * allele_freq$alf2
> # PIC per locus (biallelic SNP formula, Botstein et al. 1980):
> # PIC = 2pq(1 - pq)
> PIC_locus <- 2 * allele_freq$alf1 * allele_freq$alf2 *
+   (1 - allele_freq$alf1 * allele_freq$alf2)
> # ------------------------------------------------------------
> # 4. Combine into one locus-level diversity table
> # ------------------------------------------------------------
> diversity_table <- data.frame(
+   Locus = locNames(gl6),
+   p     = allele_freq$alf1,
+   q     = allele_freq$alf2,
+   Ho    = Ho_locus,
+   He    = He_locus,
+   PIC   = PIC_locus
+ )
> 
> summary_table <- diversity_table %>%
+   summarise(
+     Ho_min  = min(Ho, na.rm = TRUE),  Ho_max  = max(Ho, na.rm = TRUE),  Ho_mean  = mean(Ho, na.rm = TRUE),
+     He_min  = min(He, na.rm = TRUE),  He_max  = max(He, na.rm = TRUE),  He_mean  = mean(He, na.rm = TRUE),
+     PIC_min = min(PIC, na.rm = TRUE), PIC_max = max(PIC, na.rm = TRUE), PIC_mean = mean(PIC, na.rm = TRUE)
+   )
> summary_table
  Ho_min    Ho_max    Ho_mean He_min He_max   He_mean
1      0 0.1234568 0.04033348  0.095    0.5 0.3261985
    PIC_min PIC_max  PIC_mean
1 0.0904875   0.375 0.2644643

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: PIC
parts:
Hi Nigus,

Your Botstein code looks correct. The two values differ because AvgPIC is equivalent to Botstein’s PIC only when genotypes are in Hardy–Weinberg proportions. In your data, mean Ho is much lower than mean He, so the heterozygote deficit is pushing AvgPIC higher.

I’d suggest reporting Botstein’s PIC calculated separately for each population, since the calculation assumes Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium. If your samples are inbred lines, you could instead use 1 − Σp² (Anderson et al. 1993), which is the simplified form of Botstein’s PIC for homozygous lines.

Anderson, 6J A., et al. "Optimizing parental selection for genetic linkage maps." Genome 36.1 (1993): 181-186.

Cheers,

Luis
